question_text: Find the differential equation corresponding to y = acos(nx + b), where a, b are parameters.

mark_split.label: Eliminate the parameters and state the D.E.

insider_note: Only a and b are named parameters — n is treated as a fixed given constant, so it stays in the final D.E. rather than being eliminated along with a and b.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Differentiate twice
steps.margin_note: One mark. Two parameters, a and b, need two rounds of differentiation before either can be eliminated.
steps.memory_tip: The chain rule brings down a factor of n each time y = acos(nx+b) is differentiated with respect to x.
steps.why: With two arbitrary constants a and b present, one differentiation is not enough to eliminate both, so the equation is differentiated a second time to build an expression that can be compared back against the original y.
common_mistakes: Stopping after the first derivative and trying to eliminate both a and b with only one equation.
Forgetting the chain-rule factor n when differentiating sin(nx+b), writing y₁ = −a sin(nx+b) instead of −an sin(nx+b).

steps.label: Eliminate the parameters and state the D.E.
steps.margin_note: The last mark. y₂ reproduces acos(nx+b), which is exactly y from (1), multiplied by −n².
steps.memory_tip: y₂ = −n²·[acos(nx+b)] = −n²y is the key recognition — the bracket is exactly the original y.
steps.why: The second derivative reproduces the bracket acos(nx+b), which is exactly the original y from equation (1), multiplied by −n²; substituting that back in eliminates both a and b at once, since neither survives in the final relation.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as y₂ = −an²cos(nx+b) without substituting acos(nx+b) = y from (1).
Treating n as a third parameter to eliminate, when only a and b are named as parameters in the question.
